info.description: REST API for Polpo — an AI agent that manages teams of AI coding agents. Manage tasks, missions, agents, playbooks, skills, notifications, and approvals. For conversational interaction, use the OpenAI-compatible POST /v1/chat/completions endpoint.

bearerAuth.description: API key passed as a Bearer token. Configure via the apiKeys field in polpo.json or the POLPO_API_KEY environment variable.

connectors.description: Connector ids the run may use (each account of an app is its own connector, e.g. gmail-2), or "none". Absent: every connector the agent has.

connectorTools.description: Per connector id: "*" or the server's raw tool names. Narrows the agent's own connectorTools.

allowedTools.description: Built-in tools or patterns (read, bash, browser_*), not connector tools. Narrows the agent's allowedTools (or its default tools).

mode.description: org: its manager, its direct reports and the extra agents; list: only the listed agents; anyone: every agent; none: no agent (Polpo always talks to it)

agents.description: Extra agents (org) or the only agents (list)

acceptFrom.description: lines: refuse senders outside its own lines (default anyone)

targets.description: Targets it may pick (`to`): Slack channel ids, Telegram chat ids, email addresses, or "*" for any. Absent: the channel's default target only.

post.description: Polpo's primary conversational interface. Send messages in OpenAI format, receive responses in OpenAI format. Polpo runs its full 37-tool agentic loop internally — you describe what you need, Polpo handles the rest. Supports streaming (SSE) and non-streaming modes.

Requires x-session-id of an existing session. Returns { compaction } without calling the model for an answer.

200.description: Task details. `runs`: where and with what each run executed (engine polpo / claude-code / codex / opencode, model, auth kind, computer, sandbox, egress, harness session, cost, budget, status, duration), newest last. `result.stderr` of a failed task is its labelled reason (a harness error says what to change); `result.retryable: false`: it was not retried automatically (model not enabled for the account, credentials refused). `failure` sums it up: `{ reason, retryable, kind }` (kind: model_access, auth, budget, killed, assessment, error). `cost`: what every run of the task cost in all (first run, retries, continuations, directions): `{ usd, harnessUsd, modelUsd, tokens, runs, lastRunUsd, byEngine, perRun, partial, recoveredUsd? }` — `partial: true` when older runs were dropped (a task keeps its latest 20) and could not be recovered from the usage records. `approvals`: the approval gates the task met, oldest first: `{ requestId, gateId, gateName, status (pending, approved, rejected, timeout), note?, resolvedBy?, requestedAt, resolvedAt? }` — the latest resolution and its note also reach the prompt of every task that depends on it. `notReached`: a mission decision node took another branch, so the task was closed (status `done`) without running: `{ reason: "decision", node, branch, answer?, confidence?, decidedBy?, at? }` (also in `result.skipped`; tasks skipped before that field existed are recognised from their result text).

get.description: The agent as production runs it, with `versioning` (production version, latest, draft state). `view=draft`: its draft (working copy) instead, as the dashboard edits it.
Published versions, newest first (without their config: GET …/versions/{version} has it), with the production pointer and the draft's state.
A published version with its full config snapshot (read-only). `draft` and `production` are accepted too.

Per-field changes and a git-style unified diff of the serialized config between two refs: a version (1.2.0), `production` or `draft`. `to` defaults to `draft`; `from` defaults to the latest version for the draft, else the version before `to`.

delete.description: Throw away the draft's unpublished changes (production is not touched).

post.description: A draft is based on the version production ran when it started. After a rollback or deploy moved production elsewhere the draft is stale (`versioning.draft.stale`): this applies its own changes over what production runs now (or drops it when nothing is left to change).

Publish the draft as a new immutable version: the suggested bump (patch for text/prompt/identity, minor for added tools/skills/connectors/settings, major for an engine or model change or removed tools/skills/connectors) unless `bump` or `version` says otherwise. Publishing does not deploy: `deploy: true` also deploys it to production.

deploy.description: Also deploy it to production (through the deploy gate when the agent has required suites)

wait.description: With deploy: wait for the required suites to finish (default: the deploy is returned pending)

200.description: Published (and deployed, or its deploy pending / blocked by the required suites: `deployStatus`, `gate`; without deploy, `check`: the publish checks started)

409.description: No draft changes, the version exists, or the draft is stale (rebase or discard it)

post.description:
Move the production pointer to a published version: everything that runs the agent without a pinned version (chats, tasks, missions, schedules, channels, MCP, Polpo) uses it from its next run; runs in flight keep theirs. Recorded in the deploy history with who, when, from → to and the note.

**Deploy gate**: when the agent has required suites (`gate.required`), they run against the version first (trigger `deploy`) and the request answers `202` with the gate pending (`GET …/deploy-gates/{id}`, events `agent:gate`): production moves only when every one passes; otherwise the deploy is blocked and recorded in the history (`action: blocked`). `wait: true` waits for the verdict (`200` deployed, `409` `GATE_BLOCKED`). `override: { reason }` (admins only) deploys at once anyway, recording which gates had failed.

override.description: Deploy even if the required suites fail (or without running them): admins only, the reason is recorded

wait.description: Wait for the required suites (default: return the deploy pending, 202)

200.description: Deployed: the history entry, `status: deployed`, its `gate` when the suites verified it (or an override)

202.description: Pending: the required suites are running (`status: pending`, `gate`)

403.description: An override by someone who is not an admin

409.description: Blocked by the required suites (`GATE_BLOCKED`, with `data.gate`), or another version is being verified

get.description: The agent's deploy gates, newest first: the required suites run against a version before a deploy (trigger deploy / api-update) or when it is published (publish). Each: status (running — in verifica —, passed, blocked, failed, override, cancelled, errored), progress, each suite's run, pass rate, score, the reasons it failed and its failed cases, the override.
A gate with its progress (while running), each required suite's run and verdict, the deploy (or block) it led to. `wait` (seconds, up to 55): wait for it to finish first.

post.description: Stop a gate that is running: its suite runs are cancelled and nothing is deployed (production is unchanged).

409.description: Not running

post.description: Deploy a gate's version although its required suites did not pass (or are still running: they are cancelled). Admins only; the reason is mandatory. The deploy history records the override: who, when, the reason and which gates had failed.

409.description: Already deployed

post.description: Deploy the version production ran before the current one (or `to`). A rollback is a deploy: it appears in the history with its diff. It is never gated by the required suites (it must always work); a verification in flight is cancelled.

409.description: Nothing to roll back to

get.description: Every move of the production pointer, newest first: when, who, from → to, note, rollback marker; deploys the required suites blocked (`action: blocked`). Each entry verified by a deploy gate carries `gate` (status, the suites and their runs, what failed, the override). `diff=true` adds each deploy's diff (per-field changes and a unified diff of the config).
A deploy (or rollback) and the git-style diff between the version it replaced and the one it deployed.

post.description: Runs checks of everything the agent has at its disposal: engine and model (a minimal real request, a few tokens), tools, connectors, vault references (names only), skills, computer and sandbox, channels, versioning; `smoke` (only when listed) runs a tiny real chat turn that calls one harmless tool. Each check returns pass / warn / fail with its items and a fix when there is one. The run is kept in the agent's history.

checks.description: Which checks (default: all but smoke, the live run that costs a real turn)

target.description: production (default), draft, or a published version (1.2.0)

startComputer.description: Start a stopped remote computer to test it (it may cost)

smokePrompt.description: The smoke run's message (default: call one harmless tool)

get.description: The agent's test runs, newest first, with each check's result, the target and version tested and when.

post.description: Applies a one-click fix a check offered: `grant-connector-access` adds the agent to the connector's access list (the agent names the connector's tools in allowedTools but cannot see them).

get.description: The agent's test and eval suites (cases, datasets, mocks), by name.

post.description: Creates a suite: { name, description?, defaultMode (none | tools | model | all, default all), mocks?, cases: [{ name, input: { kind: chat | task, message, history?, context? }, mode?, mocks?: { tools?: [{ tool, when?, response?, error?, delayMs?, times? }], model?: { turns: [{ text?, toolCalls? }] }, unmockedTools? }, assertions: [...], dataset?, budgets? }], datasets?: [{ name, rows }] }, or { yaml } with the same in YAML. Ids are made from names when missing.

409.description: A suite with this id exists

get.description: The suite; ?format=yaml returns { yaml, revision } (the YAML view).

put.description: Replaces the suite (validated), or creates it. Send `revision` (the one you edited) to refuse the save when someone changed it meanwhile (409). Body: the suite, or { yaml, revision? }.

409.description: Changed meanwhile

delete.description: Deletes the suite (its past runs stay in the history).

post.description: Imports rows from CSV (first line: the column names; quotes, comma, semicolon or tab) or JSON (a list of objects, or { rows }) into a new dataset, or replaces / appends the rows of the dataset `id`. Cases use a dataset with `dataset: <id>` and {{row.column}} in their input, mocks and assertions.

coerce.description: CSV: numbers and booleans from text (default true)

post.description: Runs the suite (or `caseIds`) against the agent at `target` (production, draft, 1.2.0), each case a real chat turn through the agent's own path with its mocks: mode all runs offline (scripted model, mocked tools), tools mocks the tools (real model), model scripts the model (real tools), none is live. A run that uses real tools needs `allowRealTools: true` (403 otherwise); approvals are never given. `overrides` change the agent for this run only. Returns the run (running, or finished with `wait: true`); poll GET /agents/{name}/suite-runs/{runId}.

target.description: production (default), draft, or a published version (1.2.0)

mode.description: Run every case in this mode (default: each case's own): none, tools, model, all

overrides.description: Per-run changes to the agent (model, reasoning, engine, instructions, allowedTools, maxTurns): this run only

wait.description: Wait for the run to finish (default false: the run is returned running)

repetitions.description: Run every case this many times (mean, stddev and flakiness per case; default the suite's evals.repetitions, 1)

baselineRunId.description: Compare with this run instead of the suite's baseline

regressionTolerance.description: A score or pass-rate change within this is not a regression (default the suite's, 0.05)

allowRealTools.description: Confirm a run that uses real tools (modes none / model, or unmocked tools run for real): side effects are possible; approvals are never given

record.description: Record: run the cases live (real model and tools; needs allowRealTools and an admin) and save each one's exchange as its cassette (secrets redacted); the cases replay it from then on

get.description: The suite's finished runs over time, oldest first: pass rate, overall score, mean per scorer, cost, latency, regressions versus the baseline; and the same by version (production's version, a published one, or draft).

The run marked as the suite's baseline (summary, without traces), or null. Without a marked baseline, a new run is compared with the suite's policy (evals.baseline: previous — default —, production or none).

put.summary: Mark a run as the baseline
